entities.summary: Albert Benjamin Prescott was an American chemist. He graduated in medicine at the University of Michigan in 1864, and was made assistant professor of organic and applied chemistry, dean of the school of pharmacy, and director of the chemical laboratory over the years. Professor Prescott served as president of the American Chemical Society in 1886, president of the American Association for the Advancement of Science in 1891, and president of the American Pharmacists Association in 1900. During his tenure as Dean at the University of Michigan College of Pharmacy, Prescott encouraged the foundation of what is now the Phi Delta Chi professional pharmacy fraternity.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As president of the American Chemical Society and other prominent scientific organizations, Prescott played a key role in shaping the development of pharmacy education and practice in North America. His contributions to the establishment of the Phi Delta Chi fraternity helped standardize pharmacy education for decades.
